## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Upakkhata Sutta* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 8) is a disciplinary text in the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka governing the acquisition of robes by Buddhist monks [SuttaCentral]. The rule establishes that if a layperson has set aside a robe fund intended to purchase a robe for a monk, and that monk approaches the donor to request a particularly fine or expensive robe, he commits an offense requiring forfeiture of the robe (*nissaggiya*) and formal confession (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the rule and its accompanying analysis has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral indicate that this regulation forms a standard part of Buddhist monastic law across traditions, with parallel rules found in the Pātimokkhas and Vinayavibhaṅgas of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya lineages preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, Tibetan, and Gāndhārī, as well as the corresponding Pali Bhikkhunī rule (Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 18) [SuttaCentral]. Automated text reuse analysis via DharmaNexus shows widespread reuse within the Pali canon, sharing extensive textual segments with closely related robe regulations, notably Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 9 and 27, the *Bhikkhupātimokkha*, and the *Bhikkhunīpātimokkha* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language machine alignments further demonstrate substantial matches with the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003), Sanskrit *Prātimokṣasūtra*, and related monastic commentaries such as the *Pratimokṣasūtrapaddhati* and *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
